## Extract one interpretable panel family

The main Current well-being dataflow codes **Life satisfaction** as measure `11_1`. The extract below retains total-population observations when the relevant demographic dimensions are available.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
life_satisfaction <- cwb |>
  dplyr::filter(
    MEASURE == cfg$analysis$case_study$outcome_measure,
    !is.na(TIME_PERIOD_NUMERIC)
  )

for (dimension in names(cfg$analysis$panel$total_codes)) {
  if (dimension %in% names(life_satisfaction)) {
    life_satisfaction <- life_satisfaction |>
      dplyr::filter(
        .data[[dimension]] == cfg$analysis$panel$total_codes[[dimension]]
      )
  }
}

life_satisfaction |>
  dplyr::select(
    dplyr::any_of(
      c(
        "REF_AREA",
        "TIME_PERIOD",
        "MEASURE",
        "UNIT_MEASURE",
        "OBS_VALUE",
        "DOMAIN"
      )
    )
  ) |>
  utils::head(20) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

## Country trajectories


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
panelView::panelview(
  Y = "OBS_VALUE",
  data = life_satisfaction,
  index = c("REF_AREA", "TIME_PERIOD_NUMERIC"),
  type = "outcome",
  leave.gap = TRUE,
  group.mean.overlay = TRUE
)
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![Observed life-satisfaction trajectories in the total-population extract.](08-case-study_files/figure-html/life-satisfaction-trajectories-1.png){width=672}
:::
:::


This page is intentionally descriptive. A country fixed-effects regression would be easy to estimate from a panel extract, but a causal interpretation would require an identification strategy beyond the panel structure itself.
